To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of the term public in the security field is problematic.

(1) the public is a concept that is used to describe the subjects of security, but (2) this public is in(ter) visible and (3) the subjects of security are not the public but the subjects of the public.
the security and resilience discourse in the UK has become more and more complex, and that it is increasingly difficult to understand the meaning of the concepts that are used in this discourse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the ‘public’ is constituted through the use of surveillance and transparency, and how these are used in the production of the ‘public’.
how visibility and transparency are being used in the context of the EU and its external relations.
the question of how the ‘public’ is constituted as a security subject, and what this means for the possibility of ‘security’ as such.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ‘public’ is not an adequate concept for the study of security.
Barnett has made a very good start in critiquing the critical security studies literature, and in doing so has provided a useful starting point for further research.
the ‘public’ as the milieu for security and resilience is not a viable option.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ‘public’ is not a ‘milieu’ but an effect of the ‘milieu’ and as such it is not the milieu of security but the subject of it.
we are not only interested in the public as the milieu of resilience, but also in how the public is made and unmade through the processes of resilience.
we argue for a more nuanced understanding of the public, and that this can be found through an engagement with the concepts of visibility and the transparent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ‘public’ is always-already an in(ter) visible subject of security, and that the question that needs to be asked is not how to make the ‘public’ more visible but how to make security less visible.
the public is not a milieu of security.
the public is a concept that is not necessarily visible or transparent.
